'''Zoltán Füredi''' ([[Budapest]], [[Hungary]], 21 May 1954) is a [[Hungarian people|Hungarian]] mathematician, working in [[combinatorics]], mainly in [[discrete geometry]] and [[extremal combinatorics]]. He was a student of [[Gyula O. H. Katona]]. He is a corresponding member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] (2004). He is a research professor of the [[Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics|Rényi Mathematical Institute]] of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and a professor at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] (UIUC).

Füredi received his [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree in mathematics in 1981 from the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=24920}}</ref>

==Some results==
* In infinitely many cases he determined the maximum number of edges in a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] with no [[cycle graph|''C''<sub>4</sub>]].<ref name="Füredi quadrilaterals">{{cite journal | last=Füredi | first=Zoltán | title=Graphs without quadrilaterals | journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=34 | issue=2 | year=1983 | issn=0095-8956 | doi=10.1016/0095-8956(83)90018-7 | pages=187–190| doi-access=free }}</ref>
* With [[Paul Erdős]] he proved that for some ''c''>1, there are ''c''<sup>''d''</sup> points in ''d''-dimensional space such that all triangles formed from those points are [[triangle#By internal angles|acute]].
* With [[Imre Bárány]] he proved that no [[polynomial time]] algorithm determines the volume of [[convex bodies]] in dimension ''d'' within a multiplicative error ''d''<sup>''d''</sup>.
* He proved that there are at most <math>O(n\log n)</math> unit distances in a convex ''n''-gon.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Z. Füredi|title=The maximum number of unit distances in a convex n-gon|journal=[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]]|series=Series A|volume=55|issue=2|year=1990|pages=316–320|doi=10.1016/0097-3165(90)90074-7|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* In a paper written with coauthors he solved the Hungarian [[lottery]] problem.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Z. Füredi, [[Gabor Szekely|G. J. Székely]], and Z. Zubor|title=On the lottery problem|journal=Journal of Combinatorial Designs|volume=4|issue=1|year=1996|pages=5–10|doi=10.1002/(sici)1520-6610(1996)4:1<5::aid-jcd2>3.3.co;2-w}} [http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/(SICI)1520-6610(1996)4:1%3C5::AID-JCD2%3E3.0.CO;2-J/abstract] [http://www.math.uiuc.edu/~z-furedi/PUBS/furedi_lotto.pdf Reprint]</ref>
* With [[Ilona Palásti]] he found the best known lower bounds on the [[orchard-planting problem]] of finding sets of points with many 3-point lines.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Arrangements of lines with a large number of triangles|last1=Füredi|last2=Palásti|first1=Z.|first2=I.|journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=92|issue=4|pages=561–566|year=1984|jstor=2045427|doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-1984-0760946-2|doi-access=free}}.</ref>
* He proved an upper bound on the ratio between the fractional matching number and the [[Matching in hypergraphs|matching number in a hypergraph]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Füredi|first=Zoltán|date=1981-06-01|title=Maximum degree and fractional matchings in uniform hypergraphs|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02579271|journal=Combinatorica|volume=1|issue=2|pages=155–162|doi=10.1007/BF02579271|s2cid=10530732|issn=1439-6912|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
